task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about Dellmere Museum's one-year move to free general admission. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 11, 2026.

facts.text: Under the fictional Dellmere Museum's current policy, the standard general-admission ticket is $8 for visitors ages 16 and older; visitors younger than 16 enter without charge.
Its trustees voted on Sept. 10, 2026, to make general admission free for one year beginning Jan. 1, 2027.
The decision covers the permanent galleries but not separately priced workshops or visiting exhibitions with their own tickets.
The museum budget anticipates $68,000 in forgone admission income, based on its own recent accounts rather than a forecast of future attendance.
A $45,000 civic grant and $23,000 from an unrestricted reserve will cover that planned first-year income gap.
Funding beyond the first year has not been approved, and the trustees have not committed to keeping admission free permanently.
Museum director Lora Tenn said, "We want someone to be able to come back for one room, not feel they must see everything to justify a ticket."
The museum will keep a staffed welcome desk to count entries and explain which activities still need separate booking.
Entry counts will include repeat visits and will not by themselves establish the number of different people reached.
A neighborhood advisory group supported the price change but identified bus costs and limited Sunday hours as remaining access barriers.
Advisory group member Ilan Moss said, "The price at the door is one part of the journey, not the whole journey."
The approved budget does not extend opening hours, subsidize transport or add new staff positions.
The trustees will review actual entries, voluntary donations and operating costs after six months.
The museum has not predicted that extra donations or shop purchases will replace the lost admission income.
Members will retain advance booking for selected talks and the existing members' newsletter, rather than receiving an admission discount that no longer has value.
The museum will contact current members before renewal to explain the changed benefit structure.
Its permanent collection focuses on local manufacturing, river transport and domestic life, with three galleries arranged around a former engine hall.
The grant agreement requires the museum to report the trial's costs and access findings but sets no attendance target it must claim to have achieved.
The existing school-visit program remains separately scheduled and is not being replaced by ordinary walk-in admission.
A planned visiting photography exhibition in spring 2027 will retain its separate ticket because its loan and staffing costs sit outside general admission.
The trustees considered a reduced-price ticket but selected the one-year free-admission trial in the recorded decision.
The museum has not yet measured any change in audience composition or repeat visits resulting from the new policy.

forbidden_additions: Permanently free entry to every museum activity.
Guaranteed replacement income or demonstrated attendance growth.
New hours, staffing or transport support not funded in the decision.
preserve: The one-year funding arrangement and distinction between general and separately ticketed admission.
Access barriers beyond ticket price and the limited meaning of entry counts.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
